title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 sets rules for the design, use, and oversight of AI‑controlled machines and robots, aiming to keep them safe and reliable. It requires companies to register their AI systems, carry out safety tests, and work with regulators to prevent misuse and protect public interest.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The “Make AI Work for Americans Act” calls for federal policies that ensure artificial intelligence technologies benefit the entire American population. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and equitable access to AI tools and services for all citizens.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires Chinese companies to regularly report the size, capabilities, and deployment details of their AI systems to the government. It aims to monitor AI development, ensure compliance with national security and ethical standards, and regulate the use of powerful AI technologies.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits artificial intelligence from providing medical diagnoses and treatment. It requires that only qualified human doctors be authorized to offer medical care, ensuring accountability and patient safety.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: Congress proposes creating the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President to oversee AI risks and other emerging technologies. This office will monitor threats, coordinate responses, and help safeguard national security and the public interest.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law designed to promote trustworthy AI by setting strict guidelines for research and development. It mandates that AI systems be rigorously tested, transparent, and safe before being released, to protect public welfare and maintain confidence in emerging technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Act requires companies that build or use AI systems to assess and mitigate risks such as bias, safety failures, or misuse. It also creates a regulatory framework that sets security standards, audit requirements, and oversight to protect public safety and promote responsible AI deployment.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to examine how artificial intelligence can both pose threats to and enhance cybersecurity. The board will analyze incidents, recommend safeguards, and work with government agencies and private entities to protect critical infrastructure.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a specialized task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to address AI‑related security risks. It outlines strategies, guidelines, and coordination mechanisms to safeguard national infrastructure and critical systems from AI‑driven threats.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: This resolution establishes a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence to oversee and guide AI policy and its implications. The committee will evaluate AI's impacts, risks, and opportunities to ensure responsible development and use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 sets up a legal framework for assessing the safety and potential harm of AI technologies. It requires thorough risk evaluations before AI systems are deployed and establishes guidelines to ensure transparency, accountability, and mitigation of any identified risks.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to regulate the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It focuses on ensuring safety, transparency, and accountability while protecting user privacy and preventing misuse of AI technology.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act temporarily suspends the construction of new AI‑driven data centers to address environmental and regulatory concerns. It also sets standards for existing facilities to ensure they meet safety, energy‑efficiency, and compliance requirements.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 requires companies that develop or deploy AI systems to assess and mitigate their environmental footprints, including energy consumption and electronic waste. The act establishes reporting standards, carbon reduction goals, and incentives for green AI practices to help reduce the sector's overall ecological impact.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed federal law that aims to help students understand artificial intelligence and be ready to use it safely and responsibly. It would create guidelines and provide resources so schools can add AI lessons to their regular curriculum, giving kids the digital skills they’ll need for the future.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a U.S. law aimed at ensuring AI systems are trustworthy and safe. It establishes funding, oversight, and standards for AI research to prevent harm and promote reliable, ethically aligned technology.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to create a pilot program that uses artificial intelligence to help defend critical infrastructure from cyber threats. This initiative is part of broader efforts to strengthen national cyber resilience and improve protection of essential systems.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to weave artificial intelligence education into school curricula so that students can understand, assess, and responsibly use AI technologies. It also sets standards and provides resources for schools, teachers, and communities to build AI literacy and prepare students for an increasingly AI‑driven future.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a law that requires the Veterans Affairs Department to use artificial‑intelligence tools in a transparent and fair way when reviewing and processing veterans’ claims. It creates rules and oversight to make sure those tools are accurate, unbiased, and that veterans can understand how decisions about their benefits are made.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires that any artificial‑intelligence system used by the Department of Veterans Affairs be clearly identified, and that its purpose, data sources, and decision‑making logic be disclosed to patients, clinicians, and the public. It also mandates regular audits, public reporting of performance and bias metrics, and an independent oversight board to review compliance and address any concerns.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act is a proposed law that would create a nationwide effort to teach people about AI, its benefits, risks, and everyday impact. It aims to partner government, academia, and industry to develop clear resources, boost media literacy, and help citizens make informed choices about AI technologies.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution emphasizes that AI systems should respect religious freedom and consider the authority of religious texts when developed and deployed. It also calls for greater transparency in AI to ensure accountability and public trust.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to safeguard users from misleading or false AI-generated content. It sets standards for transparency, accountability, and consumer protection against deceptive AI practices.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will examine the scope and impact of AI in intelligence operations and assess compliance with legal and privacy requirements.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip the U.S. workforce with the skills needed to thrive in an AI-driven economy. It proposes expanded AI education programs, curriculum updates, and workforce development initiatives to ensure people can secure and advance in future technology jobs.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act encourages the creation and maintenance of open‑source AI systems, promoting transparency, collaboration, and accessibility across the industry. It also outlines standards and responsibilities for developers and organizations to ensure that open‑source AI tools are reliable, safe, and aligned with public interests.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law aimed at preventing artificial intelligence companies from overcharging consumers and manipulating wage levels within the AI sector. It seeks to establish regulatory measures and enforce transparency and fair pricing practices for AI products and services.
